text:
olivia: Heads-up: production p95 for /v1/stream jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms after today's deploy. First saw it at ~10:12 UTC. Rolling back? :eyes:

matt: On it. Any trace ids or spans to look at?

olivia: Trace 4f3a9c... shows long blocking in sse_send_frame -> sse_window_flush. Toolcall paths show serialization waiting on flush timer.

nina: CI perf job runtime/streaming also failed on latest main — p95 increased ~250ms in CI. Logs uploaded to gs://redwood-ci/perf/1725009/.

ci-bot: CI job runtime/streaming_perf — FAILED — p95 regression 260ms vs baseline. https://ci.redwood/test/1725009

lee: @matt can you bisect PRs from last deploy? I suspect the framing/windowing changes from that batching PR.

matt: K. Running git bisect locally. Quick skim: PR #4852 touched SSE windowing + toolcall framing headers. Trying revert locally.

olivia: KV cache hit rates look unchanged. This smells like buffering/serialization not kernel selection.

matt: Bisect narrowed it to commit 7c8a2fe — change in sse_buffering: flush_interval now rounds to 10ms instead of flushing immediately on first chunk.

nina: That would coalesce many small frames. Perf tests for us are lots of sub-100-byte toolcall responses, so head latency regress.

lee: Can we do a targeted revert for just buffering sematics? Cannot revert the whole PR atm.

matt: Pushed revert candidate: branch revert/sse-windowing-7c8a2fe. It keeps batching but special-cases frames with header "x-toolcall": true to flush immediately.

deploy-bot: Deploying revert/sse-windowing-7c8a2fe to staging...

deploy-bot: Staging deploy succeeded. Running runtime/streaming perf harness.

ci-bot: Staging perf: p95 back to baseline ~120ms. Signal looks good.

olivia: :thumbsup: Can we do a 10% canary and monitor traces for 30m before rolling further?

lee: I'll open a rollout hold and annotate: "sse windowing latency regression on small frames" — we should not proceed until canary validated.

matt: Leaving notes on PR #4852 to split buffering change from batching heuristics. Also adding unit perf tests that simulate 1-10 token messages.

nina: Added CI perf case runtime/streaming/small-toolcall-case and gated it to fail the job on regressions.

olivia: After canary, if telemetry is clean we'll merge revert + follow-up to reintroduce safe batching with explicit headers.

matt: Debug notes: traces show queue_wait up to ~280ms waiting for next flush_timer; kernel selection and execution time unchanged. Flamegraph gist: https://gist.github.com/matt/abcdef

nina: I'll add alerting to page SRE on sudden p95 spikes and include gs:// links to traces in the alert payload.

olivia: Filed rollout hold in Console. Tagging eng-sre for incident follow-up if production degrades. :handshake:

lee: FYI some clients use SSE over chunked HTTP; the new framing had subtle interaction causing timers to delay flush when chunk boundaries misalign. Worth rolling that into the postmortem.

matt: Local repro I used:
```
make run-runtime && curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -d @small-req.json http://localhost:8080/v1/stream
```
observed flush gaps matching CI traces.

olivia: Thanks — keep updates here. I'll draft infra-notice after canary completes.

deploy-bot: Canary at 10% started — monitor dashboard /dash/rollouts/1823

ci-bot: Note: main is blocked by perf gate until runtime/streaming/small-toolcall-case passes in CI.

olivia: Closing loop: revert merged to main, canary validated, unblocked once CI gate added. Will follow up with short postmortem and action items.
